[[Image:Calculator_hp38g.jpg|thumb|250px|right|HP 38G]]
The '''HP&nbsp;38G''' (F1200A, F1892A) is a programmable [[graphing calculator]] by [[Hewlett-Packard]] (HP).  It was introduced in 1995 with a [[suggested retail price]] of {{US$|80|1995|round=-1}}. HP credits a committee of eight high school, [[community college]], and university teachers with assisting in the design of the calculator.

The calculator is derived from and the [[HP Saturn|hardware]] is based on the more powerful science/engineering oriented [[HP&nbsp;48 series]] of machines.

Unlike the HP&nbsp;48 series, which offered both [[reverse Polish notation]] and algebraic entry logic, the HP&nbsp;38G has only algebraic entry. The calculator is programmable, supporting small, interactive applications called "aplets".

==Successors==
After a '''HP&nbsp;38G+'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hpmuseum.org/forum/thread-845-post-9199.html#pid9199|title=Multiplication Poll: * or · or something else?}}</ref> prototype was cancelled in 1998, the 38G was replaced in 2000 by the [[HP&nbsp;39G]] and (in Europe and some other markets) [[HP&nbsp;40G]]. The two models were differentiated by the inclusion of a [[Computer Algebra System|computer algebra system]] (CAS) in the HP&nbsp;40G. An unofficial method of operating the 40G's CAS on the 39G was addressed in the next follow-up device, the [[HP&nbsp;39g+]] introduced in 2003, for which there is no known CAS implementation.

Further successors have included the [[HP&nbsp;39gs]] and [[HP&nbsp;40gs]] (with and without CAS) introduced in 2006, and the [[HP&nbsp;39gII]] in 2011.

Beginning with the 39g+, all of these successors have been built using an [[ARM architecture]] CPU with varying degrees of emulation to support software written for previous members of the series, and have gradually added more modern methods of connectivity such as [[USB]] to either replace or supplement the original [[RS-232]] and [[Infrared#Communications|IR]].
